messages:
Sara Li: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking we should tighten the public API for fused QKV to reduce per-request branching in the runtime. Proposal: make Rope/bias/dropout choices explicit at compile time and expose a small set of curated fused variants rather than a single ‘do-everything’ kernel. Thoughts?

Michael Park: +1 to moving flags to compile-time. If ModelMeta advertises features (rope, bias, dropout) we can select the kernel once during graph compilation rather than at every call. saves a ton of branching. :+1:

Andy Chen: I like curated variants. Suggest two levels: `fused_qkv_fast` (no bias, rope off, dropout stripped) and `fused_qkv_compat` (supports bias/rope but slower). That makes testing & perf regressions obvious. Example registration: 
```
model.register_kernel("fused_qkv_fast", features={"bias":false,"rope":false,"dropout":false})
model.register_kernel("fused_qkv_compat", features={"bias":true,"rope":true,"dropout":true})
```

Dmitri Volk: Concern: streaming + KV caching has semantics that sometimes require bias/rope even if model meta says no (legacy exports, patched weights). We need a cheap runtime gate for fused usage (e.g., contiguous KV, no nonstandard rotary params). Pseudo: `can_use_fused = !has_noncontiguous_kv && seq_len <= kernel_max && rope_mode == expected` — if false, fall back to slow path.

Sara Li: Good call. I want to avoid per-token checks though. Can the gate be evaluated once per request at start and baked into the execution plan? That way we don't pay per-token.

Michael Park: Yes — evaluate at request start during plan generation. The plan picks a kernel id and that kernel is used for the whole stream. If stream changes shape mid-request (rare), we can mark plan invalid and recompile.

Andy Chen: Rollout idea: enable `fused_qkv_fast` for 10% canary traffic on Redwood Dedicated first, with metric `fused_qkv.failure_rate` and `fused_qkv.p99_latency`. If failure_rate > 0.1% auto-disable for that customer.

Dmitri Volk: Also add `fused_qkv.kv_invalidation_count` to trace cases where KV contiguity assumption broke. Those are usually bugs in upstream exporters.

Sara Li: Agreed. Ops, can eng-sre plumb alerts for those metrics? Tagging @Michael Park for the alert runbook.

runtime-bot: [automated] perf-test: fused_qkv_fast vs compat — sampled on rtx-a100: p99 down by ~18%, avg tokens/s +22%. Full CSV: https://ci.redwood/perf/1849001234/fused_qkv.csv

Michael Park: Nice numbers. Last ops question: backward compatibility — should old exported models default to compat path?

Andy Chen: Yes. Default to compat if ModelMeta missing or version < 2.0. Add a conversion tool `rw-infer-inspect` that can annotate a model export with explicit fuse-features to opt into fast path.

Sara Li: Action items: (1) implement ModelMeta feature flags and plan-time kernel selection (2) add `fused_qkv_fast` and `fused_qkv_compat` kernels (3) `rw-infer-inspect` helper (4) dashboard + alerts for failure_rate/p99/kv_invalidation_count (5) canary rollout plan doc. I'll draft a short RFC addendum and assign owners. Thanks all. :rocket:
